scenario.common.recovery.check-device: Check {device} before relying on it again. Restored power does not confirm the equipment is working correctly.
scenario.common.recovery.handset-recharg: Phones can charge again now that power is back.
scenario.common.recovery.water-not-refil: Power is back, but used stored water is not replaced. {stored} gallons are left.
scenario.common.relocation.blocked: The household tried to relocate but could not.
scenario.common.relocation.done: The household went to its agreed destination with confirmed conditions.
scenario.common.res.backup-depleted: {backup} has used its stored energy in this exercise.
scenario.common.res.device-runtime-reach: {device} has reached the runtime documented for its backup. Plan for this before it happens.
scenario.common.res.handset-depleted: In the exercise, the household's phone battery is empty. (Your real app keeps working; this is part of the practice.)
scenario.common.res.handset-recharged: A phone was recharged from a power bank. Recharges left: {charges}.
scenario.common.res.water-depleted: Stored water has run out at the planning rate of 1 gallon per person per day.
scenario.flash-flood.choice.early.leave-: Leave early for higher ground we arranged
Leaving before roads flood is the most dependable option, if transport and a destination are confirmed.
scenario.flash-flood.choice.early.monito: Stay, follow official alerts, and be ready to move
Reasonable if the home is not in a flood-prone spot. Be ready to go to higher ground.
scenario.flash-flood.choice.early.prompt: Rain is heavy and a watch is issued. What now?
scenario.flash-flood.choice.warning.driv: Drive across the low-water crossing because it looks shallow
Turn around, don't drown. Never drive or walk through flood water (NWS).
scenario.flash-flood.choice.warning.high: Stay off the roads and move to higher ground or a higher floor; follow official instructions
Good. Do not enter flood water. If trapped, go to the highest level, but not into a closed attic (NWS).
scenario.flash-flood.choice.warning.leav: Leave only if officials direct it, by a route without flooded crossings
Only if officials direct it. Map directions do not confirm a road is safe.
scenario.flash-flood.choice.warning.prom: A flash flood warning is issued. What does the household do?
scenario.flash-flood.debrief.1: Never drive or walk through flood water. Turn around, don't drown.
scenario.flash-flood.debrief.2: A flood map shows hazard context, not how deep water is at your home now.
scenario.flash-flood.debrief.3: Without a car, arrange a ride to higher ground before it is needed.
scenario.flash-flood.debrief.4: After a flood, a private well needs testing before you drink from it.
scenario.flash-flood.event.displacement: Water entered the home. The household cannot stay tonight.
scenario.flash-flood.event.power-cut: Power is cut to the flooded area.
scenario.flash-flood.event.warning: A flash flood warning is issued for the area.
scenario.flash-flood.event.watch: Heavy rain is forecast and a flood watch is issued (practice scenario).
scenario.flash-flood.no-crossing: Low-water crossings are closed. No route through flood water is ever planned.
scenario.flash-flood.starting: Fictional: heavy rain upstream; low-water crossings near home begin to flood.
scenario.flash-flood.summary: Heavy rain, a flash flood warning, then recovery.
scenario.flash-flood.title: Flash flood
scenario.flash-flood.well-quality-unknow: Flood water may have reached the private well. Its water quality is now unknown.
scenario.freeze-power-loss.choice.day-tw: Day two, still no power. Stay or go?
Relocate now to our agreed warm place
Relocating works only if transport and a destination with heat are confirmed.
Staying is possible only while heat, water, and essential equipment are covered.
scenario.freeze-power-loss.choice.keep-w: Run a generator in the garage or near a window
Never run a generator indoors or in a garage. Keep it outdoors at least 20 feet from windows, doors, and vents (CDC).
Gather in one room and layer clothes and blankets
A reasonable short-term step. It does not replace heat for people who are sensitive to cold or for powered equipment.
Use the oven or stove to heat the home
Never use an oven or stove to heat a home. It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning or fire (CDC).
The house is getting cold. What does the household do?
Go to the warm place we agreed on in advance
Good choice if the place and the ride are confirmed. Leaving early is safer than leaving late.
scenario.freeze-power-loss.debrief.1: Your heat, water, and essential equipment may all depend on the same power.
scenario.freeze-power-loss.debrief.2: A backup only counts if it is confirmed compatible and set up. Unknown runtime stays unknown.
scenario.freeze-power-loss.debrief.3: Never heat a home with an oven or stove, and never run a generator indoors.
scenario.freeze-power-loss.debrief.4: Restored power does not refill batteries or stored water, or confirm equipment is safe.
scenario.freeze-power-loss.event.cell-de: Cell service becomes unreliable as towers run on limited backup.
scenario.freeze-power-loss.event.cell-re: Cell service is back to normal.
scenario.freeze-power-loss.event.grid-lo: The power goes out across the area.
scenario.freeze-power-loss.event.pipes-c: Check for frozen or burst pipes before relying on taps or the well again.
scenario.freeze-power-loss.starting: Fictional: overnight temperatures well below freezing for three days. The grid goes down a few hours in.
scenario.freeze-power-loss.summary: A hard freeze followed by a multi-day power outage.
scenario.freeze-power-loss.title: Freeze with power loss
scenario.freeze-power-loss.variant.exten: Power stays out for all 72 hours
scenario.heat-grid-strain.choice.during-: Power is out and it is hot. What now?
Go to our confirmed cooled place now
Works only if transport and the destination are confirmed.
Wait at home for power to return
Without cooling, people who are sensitive to heat are at higher risk. Have a plan to leave.
scenario.heat-grid-strain.choice.hottest: Rely on a fan as the only cooling
CDC guidance: fans alone do not prevent heat illness when it is very hot. Do not count on a fan as cooling.
The hottest part of the day is coming. What is the plan?
Go to a cooled place we have confirmed
A confirmed cooled place is the most dependable option, especially for people sensitive to heat.
Stay home, close blinds, and avoid using the oven
Helpful steps while cooling works. Watch for signs of heat illness (CDC).
scenario.heat-grid-strain.debrief.1: Grid strain is not an outage, but it can turn into one.
scenario.heat-grid-strain.debrief.2: Plan a confirmed cooled place and a way to get there before it is needed.
scenario.heat-grid-strain.debrief.3: A fan is not cooling when it is very hot. Ask your care team about heat and any medications.
scenario.heat-grid-strain.debrief.4: Cooling loss also affects refrigerated medication and food.
scenario.heat-grid-strain.event.grid-str: Grid operators ask everyone to conserve power. Power is still on.
scenario.heat-grid-strain.event.heat-adv: A heat advisory is in effect (practice scenario).
scenario.heat-grid-strain.event.power-re: Power is restored after the rotating outage.
scenario.heat-grid-strain.event.rotating: A rotating outage cuts power to the neighborhood. (Separate from grid strain; authored for practice.)
scenario.heat-grid-strain.event.strain-e: Temperatures ease and the grid is no longer strained.
scenario.heat-grid-strain.starting: Fictional: a multi-day heat wave. Grid operators ask for conservation; on day two a rotating outage is authored for practice.
scenario.heat-grid-strain.summary: Several very hot days while the grid is strained, with one rotating outage.
scenario.heat-grid-strain.title: Heat wave with grid strain
scenario.home-fire.choice.first-move.fig: Try to put the fire out or find the hydrant
Your job is to get out. Firefighters fight the fire. The hydrant is not part of your escape.
scenario.home-fire.choice.first-move.fin: Search the house for the pet
Do not delay escape to search for pets. Tell firefighters where the pet may be.
scenario.home-fire.choice.first-move.get: Get out, close doors behind us, and go to the meeting point
Correct. Get out and stay out (USFA).
scenario.home-fire.choice.first-move.gra: Grab phones, wallets, and documents first
Do not stop for belongings. Get out immediately (USFA).
scenario.home-fire.choice.first-move.pro: The smoke alarm sounds. What is the first move?
scenario.home-fire.choice.outside.call-f: Call 911 from outside and tell firefighters who may still be inside
Correct. Stay out and give firefighters the information.
scenario.home-fire.choice.outside.go-bac: Go back in for someone or something
Never go back inside a burning home (USFA).
scenario.home-fire.choice.outside.prompt: Everyone who could get out is at the meeting point. What now?
scenario.home-fire.debrief.1: Know two ways out of every room, and check that both are real, usable exits.
scenario.home-fire.debrief.2: Have one outside meeting point everyone knows.
scenario.home-fire.debrief.3: Plan who helps each person who needs help. Helpers never go back inside.
scenario.home-fire.debrief.4: Get out and stay out. Do not stop for belongings or pets.
scenario.home-fire.debrief.5: This is a practice route under these assumptions, not a real-time safest route.
scenario.home-fire.event.alarm: The smoke alarm sounds (practice scenario). Everyone heads for their usual exit.
scenario.home-fire.event.contacts: Call your out-of-area contact. 211 Texas can help find local services.
scenario.home-fire.event.displacement: The home cannot be used tonight.
scenario.home-fire.event.fire-origin: Smoke and fire block the kitchen (authored for practice).
scenario.home-fire.event.second-blocked: Smoke now also blocks the exit people were using (authored for practice).
scenario.home-fire.meeting-point-missing: No outside meeting point has been confirmed.
scenario.home-fire.route.alternative: {person}'s usual way out is blocked. The practice route now leaves through the {exitRoom}.
scenario.home-fire.route.no-usual: {person} has no verified way out in the home model.
scenario.home-fire.route.none: {person} has no verified practice route under these assumptions. Follow your emergency plan and call 911 from outside if you can.
scenario.home-fire.route.still-clear: {person}'s practice route out through the {exitRoom} is still clear in this exercise.
scenario.home-fire.starting: Fictional: a smoke alarm sounds. The fire starts in the kitchen (authored for practice; no fire spread is simulated).
scenario.home-fire.summary: A practice escape: smoke alarm, a blocked exit, then the night after.
scenario.home-fire.title: Home fire
scenario.home-fire.variant.second-exit-b: The second exit is also blocked
scenario.tornado.choice.warning.drive-to: Drive to a community shelter across town
Do not try to travel during a warning. The roads are not known to be safe (NWS).
scenario.tornado.choice.warning.go-outsi: Do not go outside to look. Take shelter now.
scenario.tornado.choice.warning.go-to-sh: Go to our chosen interior room on the lowest floor
Go immediately. An interior room is not an engineered safe room, but it is the planned location (NWS).
scenario.tornado.choice.warning.prompt: A tornado warning is issued. What does the household do?
scenario.tornado.choice.warning.stay-in-: Stay in the bedroom near the windows
Stay away from windows. Go to the chosen interior room.
scenario.tornado.choice.watch.leave-for-: Go now to the sturdy building we arranged
The right move from a manufactured home, if the destination and ride are confirmed before a warning.
scenario.tornado.choice.watch.prepare: Confirm our shelter spot, charge phones, keep shoes nearby
scenario.tornado.choice.watch.prepare.fe: Good. Preparation during a watch makes the warning response faster.
scenario.tornado.choice.watch.prompt: A tornado watch is issued. What does the household do now?
scenario.tornado.choice.watch.wait.feedb: Waiting leaves less time to act if a warning comes.
scenario.tornado.debrief.1: Choose the shelter room before a warning, on the lowest floor and away from windows.
scenario.tornado.debrief.2: Manufactured homes do not protect against tornadoes. Arrange a sturdy building in advance.
scenario.tornado.debrief.3: Make sure a warning can wake you at night: a charged phone with alerts, or a weather radio.
scenario.tornado.debrief.4: Do not travel to a distant shelter once a warning is issued.
scenario.tornado.event.displacement: The home is damaged and cannot be used tonight.
scenario.tornado.event.grid-down: Power is out after the storm.
scenario.tornado.event.warning: A tornado warning is issued for your location.
scenario.tornado.event.watch: A tornado watch is issued for the area (practice scenario).
scenario.tornado.manufactured-home: A manufactured home does not protect against a tornado (NWS). The plan must be to leave for a sturdy building during the watch, before a warning.
scenario.tornado.night-alert-received: The warning reaches the household at night.
scenario.tornado.night-alert-uncertain: It is not confirmed that a warning would wake the household at night.
scenario.tornado.night-alert-via.phone: It arrived as an alert on a charged phone.
scenario.tornado.night-alert-via.radio: It arrived on the battery or hand-crank weather radio.
scenario.tornado.shelter-not-chosen: No shelter location has been chosen. Deciding during a warning costs time.
scenario.tornado.shelter-preselected: The household goes to its chosen shelter location: {room}. (Not an engineered safe room.)
scenario.tornado.starting: Fictional: a tornado watch in the afternoon, then a warning for your area.
scenario.tornado.summary: A tornado watch, then an immediate warning, then recovery.
scenario.tornado.title: Tornado
scenario.tornado.variant.home-damaged: Home is damaged and cannot be used
scenario.water-outage.boil.not-feasible: Boiling is not an option here.
scenario.water-outage.choice.drinking-wa: Only for a boil-water advisory, and only with a working heat source. Boiling does not fix chemical contamination (CDC).
Do not use tap water against the advisory.
How does the household get drinking water?
Stored water is the dependable option for drinking and cooking.
scenario.water-outage.debrief.1: Different advisories mean different things. Follow the utility's exact instructions.
scenario.water-outage.debrief.2: Boiling helps only for a boil-water advisory and needs a working heat source.
scenario.water-outage.debrief.3: Boiling does not remove chemicals. Do-not-drink and do-not-use advisories need other water.
scenario.water-outage.debrief.4: Plan stored water for drinking, cooking, pets, and hygiene.
scenario.water-outage.event.advisory-lif: The utility lifts the advisory. Follow its flushing instructions.
scenario.water-outage.event.boil-advisor: The utility issues a boil-water advisory.
scenario.water-outage.event.do-not-drink: The utility issues a do-not-drink advisory.
scenario.water-outage.event.do-not-use: The utility issues a do-not-use advisory.
scenario.water-outage.event.main-break: A water main break cuts water to the area (practice scenario).
scenario.water-outage.event.well-pump-fa: The private well pump fails (practice scenario).
scenario.water-outage.event.well-quality: The well's water quality is unknown until it is tested.
scenario.water-outage.starting: Fictional: a nearby main break cuts water pressure. Later the utility issues an advisory.
scenario.water-outage.summary: A water main break, then a utility advisory.
scenario.water-outage.title: Water outage
service.alerts.operational: The household can receive official alerts again.
service.alerts.unavailable: The household can no longer receive official alerts: no charged phone with service and no confirmed weather radio.
service.alerts.unknown: It is unknown whether the household can receive official alerts.
service.cooling.degraded: Cooling is running under grid strain. Conservation requests may limit it.
service.cooling.operational: Cooling is working again in this exercise.
service.cooling.unavailable: Cooling stopped. The household no longer has access to cooling at home.
service.cooling.unknown: Cooling: the outcome is unknown because a fact is unconfirmed.
service.device.degraded: {device}: power is reduced or only partly covered.
service.device.on-backup: {device} is running on {backup}. How long it can run is only known if documented by the manufacturer or care plan.
service.device.operational: {device} has power again. Check it before relying on it.
service.device.unavailable: {device} has lost power and nothing confirmed keeps it running. This is a continuity-planning gap.
service.device.unknown: {device}: it is not confirmed that anything will keep it working. Treat this as a gap until confirmed.
service.heat.degraded: Heating is reduced in this exercise.
service.heat.operational: Heating is working again in this exercise.
service.heat.unavailable: Heating stopped: it depends on electricity in this home and no confirmed backup runs it.
service.heat.unknown: Heating may or may not keep working: it is not yet confirmed whether the furnace needs electricity for controls or a blower.
service.power.home.degraded: The grid is strained. Power is still on, but conservation is requested and an outage is possible.
service.power.home.operational: Home power is working again in this exercise.
service.power.home.unavailable: Home power is out. Only items with a confirmed, compatible backup keep running.
service.power.home.unknown: Home power: the outcome is unknown because a fact is unconfirmed.
service.refrigeration.degraded: Refrigerator and freezer is reduced in this exercise.
service.refrigeration.operational: Refrigerator and freezer is working again in this exercise.
service.refrigeration.unavailable: The refrigerator and freezer have no power. The 4-hour refrigerator planning milestone from CDC guidance starts now.
service.refrigeration.unknown: Refrigerator and freezer: the outcome is unknown because a fact is unconfirmed.
service.transport.degraded: Roads are affected. Some routes are closed or unsafe; map directions do not confirm a road is passable.
service.transport.operational: Transportation is working again in this exercise.
service.transport.unavailable: No confirmed way to travel right now.
service.transport.unknown: Transportation: the outcome is unknown because a fact is unconfirmed.
service.water.safety.degraded: Tap water is under an advisory. Follow the utility's exact instructions.
service.water.safety.operational: Tap water safety is working again in this exercise.
service.water.safety.unavailable: Tap water must not be used as the advisory states.
service.water.safety.unknown: Tap water quality is unknown. Do not assume it is safe to drink.
service.water.supply.degraded: Tap water supply is reduced in this exercise.
service.water.supply.operational: Tap water supply is working again in this exercise.
service.water.supply.unavailable: No water from the taps. The household now relies on confirmed stored water.
service.water.supply.unknown: Tap water supply is uncertain in this exercise.
service.wellPump.degraded: Well pump is reduced in this exercise.
service.wellPump.operational: Well pump is working again in this exercise.
service.wellPump.unavailable: The private well pump stopped, so the taps will run dry once any pressure-tank water is used. Stored water is tracked separately.
service.wellPump.unknown: It is not confirmed whether the well pump needs electricity, so tap water is uncertain.
service.wifi.degraded: Home Wi-Fi is reduced in this exercise.
service.wifi.operational: Home Wi-Fi is working again in this exercise.
service.wifi.unavailable: Home Wi-Fi is down because the router has no power. Cellular service is separate.
service.wifi.unknown: Home Wi-Fi: the outcome is unknown because a fact is unconfirmed.
